findings.reason: §3 and §6 should name the supervisor/reaper/placement owner each extends, and §4 should name `fleet_migrate.py`, so implementers extend the existing mechanism instead of adding a fourth parallel one.
findings.text: §2's prior-art pass stops at four files, and every mechanism §3 and §6 add has a nearer owner the plan never cites: the per-run supervisor that already holds the worker's parentage and its exit (`reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2078 _start_supervisor`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:1853 _supervisor_argv`, entry `reckon/crew/supervisor_main.py:23`, described in `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:6`); an in-process reaper and subreaper (`reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:349 _reap_launched_workers`, `:379 _worker_reaper_loop`, `:399 _ensure_launched_worker_reaper`, `:2984 prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER)`); a session host that supervises children and settles their status (`reckon/crew/session_host.py:273 SessionHost`, `:530 waitpid`, `:258 _set_parent_death_signal`); a whole-run signaller (`reckon/crew/process_signal.py:396 signal_worker` with `reach_run`); a step-argv owner (`reckon/crew/placement.py:233 step_prefix`); an existing memory default surface (`reckon/crew/fleet_node.py:44 DEFAULT_MEMORY = "96G"`, `:124 environ.get(MEMORY_ENV)`, `reckon/crew/placement.py:220 reservation_options(memory_gb=…)`); and the migrate owner (`reckon/crew/fleet_migrate.py:864`), which §4 describes as "the same file pair" as status when migrate lives in `fleet_migrate.py` and status in `reckon/crew/fleet_node.py:491`.

findings.reason: either §3 extends the supervisor with cgroup-drain-and-wait semantics, or it must state why the supervisor cannot run inside the step.
findings.text: §3 adds a reaper as "the worker step's first process" that on SIGTERM signals the worker's group, waits for every process, and exits carrying the worker's status; that is precisely what the per-run supervisor already does (it "holds a dispatched worker's parentage so its exit can be collected", installs SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers per `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2188 _worker_default_signals`, and composes an exit record from `os.waitpid`), so the section wraps existing machinery without the "why can the supervisor not be extended" sentence the rubric requires.

findings.reason: without naming one owner, the bound is added to one prefix and silently absent from the other, and a fourth supervisor accrues beside three existing ones.
findings.text: §6 places every worker step with an explicit `--mem`, but the step-argv prefix already has two owners — `reckon/crew/placement.py:233 step_prefix` (used at `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:1115`) and `reckon/crew/fleet_node.py:358 placement_argv` (used by `reckon/crew/fleet_migrate.py:238,546,579,997,1097,1184`) — so the plan must name which one carries the bound and fold the other into it; §3 likewise adds a reaper beside the supervisor owner named above.

findings.reason: the section should say whether the bound is a new dispatch option or a reuse of the existing memory default surface, which decides whether cli_options grows.
findings.text: §6 introduces a per-dispatch memory bound ("a node whose work needs more declares it at dispatch") and §4 adds a new migrate branch, and neither section names what it retires or merges, or states why nothing can be; §6 could fold the declaration into the existing run record and the pre-existing memory vocabulary (`reckon/crew/fleet_node.py:44 DEFAULT_MEMORY`, `reckon/crew/placement.py:220 memory_gb`) rather than adding a new dispatch surface to the cli_options family (362).

response_events.reason: §6 reuses the dispatch --set override and existing memory vocabulary, adding no option; §4 states it adds and retires no option

interface_budget-1.reason: §6 reuses the dispatch --set override and existing memory vocabulary, adding no option; §4 states it adds and retires no option

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan names no new module, and each section changes behaviour in an existing owner, so there is no new public interface to judge for depth; the reuse failure is scored under reuse_search and duplicate_owner.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §6's per-step memory bound and §3's reaper each land beside an existing owner that must be extended rather than forked, and the step-argv prefix the plan would put `--mem` on already has two owners.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1802, cli_options 362, mcp_views 34, refusal_families 23; §6 adds a per-dispatch memory declaration and §4 adds a migrate branch, and neither §6 nor §4 names anything it retires or merges, or states why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 cites `dispatch_launch.py`, `process_signal.py`, `fleet_node.py` and `placement.py`, but §3's reaper and §6's per-step memory bound are proposed without citing the per-run supervisor, the session host, or the existing reaper/subreaper machinery that already perform those roles.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3's reaper re-implements the signal-worker, wait-for-exit and record-status role the per-run supervisor (`reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2078`, entry `reckon/crew/supervisor_main.py:23`) already holds, with no statement of why that supervisor cannot be extended instead.
